# Feature Specification: Spec Problem Statement Section

**Feature Branch**: `006-spec-problem-statement`

**Created**: 2026-08-08

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Add a problem statement section to the spec template so specs read like proper PRDs with clear pain points, affected users, and why existing solutions fall short"

## Problem Statement *(mandatory)*

**Pain Point**: Feature specifications generated by the Spec Kit workflow jump straight into user stories and requirements without establishing *why* the feature exists. Without a clear problem statement, specs lack the context needed to evaluate whether the proposed solution addresses the right problem, leading to misaligned implementations and wasted effort.

**Who**: Bundle authors and product stakeholders who use the Spec Kit specify-plan-tasks-implement workflow. Authors struggle to frame the problem before diving into solutions; reviewers lack the "why" context when evaluating specs.

**Current Alternatives**: Currently, the problem context is either buried in the user description input field (a single free-text line), scattered across user stories, or lost entirely. There is no dedicated, structured section that forces authors to articulate the pain point, the affected audience, and why the status quo is insufficient. Reviewers must reconstruct the problem from fragments.

**Desired Outcome**: Every generated spec includes a structured problem statement that clearly identifies the pain point, who experiences it, why current alternatives fall short, and what success looks like — making specs self-contained PRDs that can be evaluated on their own merits.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Auto-Generated Problem Statement (Priority: P1)

A bundle author runs `/speckit-specify` with a natural-language feature description. The AI reads the updated spec template and automatically fills in the Problem Statement section with structured pain point, audience, current alternatives, and desired outcome derived from the description.

**Why this priority**: This is the core value — if the template section isn't picked up and filled by the specify skill, the feature delivers nothing.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by running `/speckit-specify` with a feature description and verifying the output `spec.md` contains a populated Problem Statement section with all four sub-fields filled in (not placeholders).

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a project with the updated spec template, **When** a user runs `/speckit-specify` with a feature description, **Then** the generated `spec.md` contains a Problem Statement section with Pain Point, Who, Current Alternatives, and Desired Outcome fields filled with content derived from the description.
2. **Given** a feature description that is vague about the audience, **When** `/speckit-specify` runs, **Then** the AI makes an informed guess for the "Who" field and documents the assumption in the Assumptions section.

---

### User Story 2 - Problem Statement Validates Against Checklist (Priority: P2)

After the spec is generated, the quality validation checklist confirms that the Problem Statement section is complete and contains no implementation details.

**Why this priority**: Validation ensures the section meets quality standards, but the section must exist first (P1).

**Independent Test**: Can be tested by generating a spec and checking that the validation pass includes Problem Statement completeness.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a generated spec with a complete Problem Statement, **When** the quality validation runs, **Then** the Problem Statement passes all mandatory-section checks.
2. **Given** a generated spec where the Problem Statement has a placeholder field, **When** the quality validation runs, **Then** the validation flags the incomplete field.

---

### User Story 3 - Template Backward Compatibility (Priority: P3)

Existing specs created before this change continue to work with all Spec Kit commands (plan, tasks, implement, converge, analyze) without errors, even though they lack a Problem Statement section.

**Why this priority**: Important for adoption safety, but lower priority since existing specs are already written and won't be re-generated.

**Independent Test**: Can be tested by running `/speckit-plan` or `/speckit-tasks` against an existing spec that lacks the Problem Statement section and verifying no errors occur.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a spec created before the Problem Statement section was added, **When** any downstream Spec Kit command is run against it, **Then** the command completes without errors.

### Edge Cases

- What happens when the user description is so brief that no meaningful problem statement can be inferred? The AI should make a best-effort guess and flag with [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] only if the pain point is truly ambiguous.
- What happens when a user manually removes the Problem Statement section from a generated spec? Downstream commands should not fail — the section is mandatory for generation but not enforced at consumption time.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The spec template MUST include a Problem Statement section with four structured sub-fields: Pain Point, Who, Current Alternatives, and Desired Outcome.
- **FR-002**: The Problem Statement section MUST appear after the header metadata and before User Scenarios & Testing in the template.
- **FR-003**: The specify skill MUST populate all four Problem Statement sub-fields from the user's feature description.
- **FR-004**: The specify skill MUST derive Problem Statement content from the feature description without requiring additional user input (unless a [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] is warranted).
- **FR-005**: The quality validation checklist MUST verify that the Problem Statement section is complete.
- **FR-006**: Downstream Spec Kit commands MUST NOT fail when processing specs that lack a Problem Statement section (backward compatibility).

### Key Entities

- **Spec Template**: The markdown template file (`.specify/templates/spec-template.md`) that defines the structure of generated specifications. Now includes a Problem Statement section.
- **Problem Statement**: A structured section with four sub-fields that captures why a feature exists, who needs it, and what success looks like.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of newly generated specs contain a populated Problem Statement section with all four sub-fields filled (no placeholders remaining).
- **SC-002**: Spec reviewers can understand the "why" behind a feature by reading only the Problem Statement section, without needing to parse user stories or requirements.
- **SC-003**: Zero downstream command failures when processing specs created before this change (backward compatibility).
- **SC-004**: The Problem Statement section adds less than 30 seconds to the spec generation time.

## Assumptions

- The specify skill processes the template generically (fills all sections it finds) rather than having hardcoded section awareness — validated by reading the skill source.
- The Problem Statement section uses the same HTML comment annotation pattern as other template sections.
- Existing downstream commands (plan, tasks, implement, converge, analyze) do not require specific sections to be present and will gracefully handle missing sections.
- The template change is the only production change needed — no skill code modifications are required for P1.
